title: Etale approximation of a smooth formal point at prescribed precision
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\widehat R=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}R/\mathfrak m^r$ be its maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $B$ be a commutative $R$-algebra such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix an $R$-algebra homomorphism $w:B\to\widehat R$ and an integer $N\geq1$. Write $\pi_N:\widehat R\to R/\mathfrak m^N$ for the coordinate projection. There exist an etale $R$-algebra $E$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $t:B\to E$ such that the structural map $\alpha:R/\mathfrak m^N\to E/\mathfrak m^NE$ is an isomorphism and $q_Nt=\alpha\pi_Nw$, where $q_N:E\to E/\mathfrak m^NE$ is the quotient map. Moreover $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak mE$ is a maximal ideal contracting to $\mathfrak m$, its structural residue-field map $R/\mathfrak m\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and, for $T=E_{\mathfrak q}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qT=\mathfrak mT$, one has
$$\widehat\lambda(w(z))-\iota_T(t(z)/1)\in\mathfrak n^N\widehat T\qquad(z\in B).$$
Here $\iota_T:T\to\widehat T$ is the completion map and $\widehat\lambda:\widehat R\to\widehat T$ is induced coordinatewise by the local structure map $R\to T$.

source.place: Tag 07QZ, theorem-approximation-property-variant, smooth-factorization proof: lift the smooth section. Agent refinement at precision N using the quotient by the Nth maximal-ideal power and coordinatewise completion congruences.

proof.text: Put $J=\mathfrak m^N$ and $\sigma=\pi_N\circ w:B\to R/J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-section-etale-lift] with $A=R$, this ideal $J$, and the given smooth $R$-algebra $B$. It gives an etale $R$-algebra $E$, an $R$-algebra map $t:B\to E$, and the structural isomorphism $\alpha:R/\mathfrak m^N\xrightarrow{\sim}E/\mathfrak m^NE$, with $q_Nt=\alpha\pi_Nw$. The lifting lemma allows any ideal; no henselian or G-ring hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 07M7, lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism, applied to the Nth maximal-ideal power; compare smoothing.tex Tag 07QZ, smooth-factorization paragraph

proof.text: Reducing the structural isomorphism $\alpha$ further by the ideal generated by $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^N$ gives the structural isomorphism $R/\mathfrak m\cong E/\mathfrak mE$: explicitly, $\alpha$ and its inverse preserve all products with elements of $\mathfrak m$, so descend to inverse quotient maps. Thus $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak mE$ is maximal and its inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak m$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $T=E_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qT=\mathfrak mT$. Modulo this ideal its fractions are fractions in the field $E/\mathfrak q$, and every denominator is nonzero; therefore $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=T/\mathfrak n\cong E/\mathfrak q\cong R/\mathfrak m$, via the structural maps. In particular $R\to T$ is local.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization; Tag 07BH, local rings and residue fields; elementary reduction of the isomorphism from step 1

proof.text: Write $\lambda:R\to T$ for the structural map. Since $\lambda(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, each quotient map $\lambda_r:R/\mathfrak m^r\to T/\mathfrak n^r$ is well-defined. These maps commute with reduction, so applying them to compatible sequences defines $\widehat\lambda:\widehat R\to\widehat T$, by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. In particular $\pi^T_N\widehat\lambda=\lambda_N\pi_N$. There is also a map $\beta:E/\mathfrak m^NE\to T/\mathfrak n^N$, sending the class of $e$ to the class of $e/1$, since $\mathfrak m^NT=\mathfrak n^N$. On representatives in $R$ one has $\beta\alpha=\lambda_N$. Applying $\beta$ to step 1 yields $\pi^T_N(\iota_T(t(z)/1))=\lambda_N\pi_Nw(z)=\pi^T_N(\widehat\lambda(w(z)))$ for every $z\in B$.

source.place: Tag 00M9, section-completion: compatible sequences and coordinate maps; elementary quotient calculation

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated since $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. If $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ generate it, their images generate $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mT$; thus $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated even without proving that $T$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] to $(A,I)=(T,\mathfrak n)$. It identifies $\ker(\pi^T_N)$ with $\mathfrak n^N\widehat T$. The equality of the two coordinates in step 3 therefore gives exactly $\widehat\lambda(w(z))-\iota_T(t(z)/1)\in\mathfrak n^N\widehat T$ for every $z\in B$.
